title: Emergence: A 150-Year-Old Idea Borrowed by Tech
explainer: The word "emergent," used for patterns that appear from many small interacting components without being designed in from the top, did not originate in software. Philosopher G. H. Lewes coined the term in 1875 for effects that cannot be reduced to their parts, and physicist Philip Anderson revived the idea for science broadly in his influential 1972 essay "More Is Different," arguing that complex systems develop genuinely new behavior at larger scales. Noticing an "emergent" pattern in a codebase or ecosystem is applying that older observation to a new domain.
